quest.title: Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones
quest.description: The Duke, Wriothesley, holds all the Fortress's secrets. You plan to ask him directly and get some grasp of the current situation.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x850, Mora x36825, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I—I'm so sorry, Lyney...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: I'm also really sorry, Lyney. I should have been more careful.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Don't say that. It was all my fault... I was the one who should have been more careful. You two were nearly...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: If I was stronger... Maybe I would have already found Master Childe...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: No, how can you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: What I'm hearing is, we all dropped the ball at some point during the mission, so the responsibility falls on all of us. Isn't that right?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right. It's on all of us.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Lyney, we understand that you're worried about us, but we're worried about you as well. Please don't blame yourself... We want you to keep your spirits up.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Excuse me~

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I take it Mr. Freminet's condition has stabilized?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Of course. I would not have left the infirmary otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I've been expecting those two, but might I enquire as to the purpose of your visit, Miss Sigewinne?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I wanted to check up on Miss Clorinde. How are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Mostly fine, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: If you don't mind, I'd like to perform another quick physical exam. It'll just take a few minutes.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Alright, thank you for looking out for me. I'll take my leave for now, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, want to explain yourself, Wriothesley?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Haha, of course, but I'm not partial to the word choice of "explain." How about "enlighten"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please enlighten us as much as you'd like.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: But where should I begin? How about you start by asking me any questions you have? You can start with whichever one you'd like to get answered the most.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Then Paimon will begin. Did you know about Lyney's goals from the very beginning?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: No, I just knew they were Fatui operatives sent to the Fortress by The Knave. As for their specific goals... I only figured those out as you made progress on your investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You managed to monitor and stay ahead of them even though you didn't know what they were trying to do?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: They came here with ulterior motives. I'm quite adept at discerning what that kind of behavior signals.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why didn't you stop them?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Initially, I thought their goal was just to investigate Childe's disappearance.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Lyney suggested that I had deliberately let him escape, but in truth, I didn't really do anything special to help or hinder him while he was here. Everything he did, from finding helpers to leaving this place, he did on his own.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Of course, it's inevitable that The Knave would make a big deal out of her fellow Harbinger's unexplained disappearance.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I'm also quite curious about where that Harbinger went, so I figured I might as well let the Fatui do their own investigative work. All I care about is the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you were hoping Lyney's group would just do your work for you...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: You make it sound like that's a bad thing... Unfortunately, things didn't go as planned. I assume that Freminet has told you already — the ratio of Primordial Seawater around the Fortress of Meropide is on the rise.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The forbidden zone has always been Lyney's target, and you got roped into that investigation after running into him. I began to intervene out of concern for your safety, and also to prevent the Fortress from becoming entangled in more irksome matters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are the rumors true? That you're also a former criminal?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Why would you put it like that? Isn't staying here all day and serving as the manager of the Fortress a kind of sentence unto itself, another form of prison? I just happen to have some support from the rest of the inmates, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh right, Paimon wanted to ask — who invited Clorinde down here?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Me, of course. I paid her good Mora to come down to the Fortress for some field work.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: As a Champion Duelist, Miss Clorinde can be considered to be an independent party. I needed to find an exceptionally capable person to help me get through the impending crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And saving Freminet was part of that crisis?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: You can think of it like that, yes. Credit where credit is due, that boy is quite adept at diving. Had conditions not been as hostile as they were, he probably would have found the missing Harbinger already.

choices.text: So, the forbidden zone really exists?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: That's not something you should be asking after. Neuvillette only asked you to investigate Childe's whereabouts.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: All I need to prove to you is that the forbidden zone had nothing to do with the Harbinger's disappearance. That should be clear now that you've spoken to Freminet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... we've already uncovered that there's something wrong with the infirmary, and we've answered a bunch of questions that you threw at us... Isn't it about time that you answer our last question in return?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: You make a compelling case... Do you really want to know the answer that badly?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Paimon really wants to know!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Even if the truth may not be pleasant?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Yes.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a hidden door here!? And a whole basement behind it? You're pretty good at hiding stuff, Wriothesley.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It seems you've forgotten just what kind of place the Fortress of Meropide is.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Stand on the central plate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is there a secret mechanism or — whoa!!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Once everyone has taken their positions on the circular plate, it begins to slowly move downwards...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the "forbidden zone"? Honestly, for a place so well-hidden, Paimon sure doesn't see anything special...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And that is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a huge door!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: There are three such isolation gates in total. Generally speaking, I'm the only one who's allowed to go inside. Hence the name, "forbidden zone."

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Am I correct to assume you're going to run on back and tell your little Fatui friends everything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, er, Paimon wasn't thinking of keeping anything from them...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Hah. Well, I'd advise you wait until you've seen the whole truth of this place for yourself before deciding whether or not to tell them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so there's a switch on the side...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Stand back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... They all just went up one by one...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's that in the middle of the room?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Go on, have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This room is really empty with nothing in here, which is quite strange on its own. There's also a device smack dab in the middle of the room, which looks like some kind of massive sluice gate.)

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I've been interested in what lies beyond that gate ever since I assumed leadership of the Fortress of Meropide. Of course, it would be unwise to recklessly open it, but it'd also be risky and negligent to simply ignore any potential danger that could be behind it.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The readings on that dashboard haven't budged since the day when I first laid eyes on this place. But over the past year, the needle has crept upwards from its original position, likely because some parameter it's been tracking has changed, if only infinitesimally.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Normally, I would have ignored it, but I happened to have some free time when I noticed it, so I investigated. Any guesses what the reading could be tracking?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Very reasonable guesses. I've considered both of those as well. Unfortunately, our dashboard is tracking something less ordinary.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: The temperature should vary with weather and climate changes, so for something that rarely shifts, the water pressure is more likely. We ran a few tests to increase the pressure from the outside, but the readings didn't change at all.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Later on, a few more possibilities occurred to me, such as a potential connection with the Primordial Sea. I began to make a few preparations based on that hypothesis.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Over the past few days, the needle has moved again. With that and the symptoms that Freminet displayed after leaving the Fortress, I can now confidently conclude that the readings represent the concentration of Primordial Seawater in the seawater nearby.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The concentration of... Primordial Seawater!? But we're already under the sea...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: And that is precisely the problem. We're at the bottom of the sea, and now we're surrounded by toxic seawater. Somehow, Primordial Seawater got mixed in, and the concentration is steadily rising...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Primordial Seawater is continually leaking into the sea?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Yes, that's very likely.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But forget about the two of us, not even Neuvillette knows where the Primordial Sea could be, much less where we could find and plug a leak...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Seems like you've figured it out.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I believe the Primordial Sea lies directly beneath this sluice gate. For some reason, the Primordial Seawater levels have risen significantly, and it's now very close to us.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: The indicators are now red. Although the gate still stands, some Primordial Seawater has already leaked out and mixed into the sea around us.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: ...If this continues, soon it will no longer be able to hold back the Primordial Sea at all.

choices.text: And if the Primordial Sea is leaking through...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Yeah, you know what the legends say. If this place falls, then everyone in Fontaine will be turned into puddles in the span of a night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But that's just too weird! Why would the Fortress of Meropide be built right above a sluice gate for the Primordial Sea? Who built this place, anyway?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Your expression tells me you think this might be part of a vast, complicated conspiracy. To be honest, you might find the actual answer may be exceedingly boring.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: It's just that the secret of the "forbidden zone" had been long forgotten by the nation before I rediscovered it with my research.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: There's no single "founder" of the Fortress of Meropide in any traditional sense. What we know about its history has been left to us by the people who used to live here.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: When the previous Hydro Archon, Egeria, ruled the land, all convicted criminals from Fontaine were exiled. The people drove the criminals away like a wolf pack chasing away the banished.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: The criminals received no sympathy of any kind from the people. They were exiled to the desolate seaside, where they experienced only pain, struggle, and the bone-chilling cold.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Some of them began to repent, and prayed to the Hydro Archon, asking if there was still anything they could do. The Hydro Archon took pity on them, and said: You may go guard my secret, deep underneath the waves.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: And so, leaning on the power of the Hydro Archon, they gathered underneath the sea, and began to build a fortress. They became a community down there in the deeps, and over the years, helped it to grow.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: As the number of exiles increased, more and more people joined the community. When the first group of exiles died, they left the yet-unfinished fortress to their successors.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: The Hydro Archon continued to lend her support, allowing the fortress and what it stood for to continue growing ever larger. Before long, this dark underwater fortress became the sinners' only home.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: And with that, the people here stopped referring to the Fortress as a prison. They saw themselves as repenting sinners, who would regain their freedom once they had sufficiently redeemed themselves.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: But as time went on, people also realized that the Fortress was a lonely place. Once they had gotten used to life here, they could no longer feel comfortable living in the overworld.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Once they had finished serving their sentences, some people left, and some others chose to stay. They'd find some idle position, and let their withered souls fade away with the ancient secrets of the past.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: ...After many, many centuries, few people still remember the reason for the Fortress' founding. Now, they just see it as an integral pillar of Fontainian society, as the place where criminals deserve to be sent.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Now and again, researchers manage to break one law or another, and live out their days in the Fortress. I learned all this from an elderly historian — everyone else just thought he'd made it all up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But now you know, every part of that history is true...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Indeed. It's just as the prophecy says. If this gate fails, then everyone will be dissolved into the sea.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you believe in prophecies?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: To be frank, not really. But sadly, that hasn't stopped this prophecy from proving all too accurate.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Prophecies are troublesome things. Just hearing one will create the first wave of panic. Seeing signs of it will bring about the second, and actually witnessing it in real time, the third.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, as the Duke of Meropide, just what do you plan to do about it?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Let's go somewhere else. I want to show you something.

choices.text: If this gate falls, all of Fontaine will fall with it.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: This is it.

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Your Grace! Perfect timing. The results from our latest round of experiments have—

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Wait, Jurieu, he's not alone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Lourvine and Jurieu?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: No need to panic, you two. I've already told them about our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: What? After you warned us not to tell a single soul about any of this!?

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: I'm skeptical as well. Are you sure they are trustworthy?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The results speak for themselves, don't they? These two may already know more than you could ever imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: ...Alright then, if Your Grace insists.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: They seem harmless enough... So I'll trust them for now.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: How about some reintroductions... This is Jurieu, one of the highest-ranked researchers from the Fontaine Research Institute. He used to work under Edwin. I trust that you've heard of Edwin?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Good. Saves me a bit of time explaining.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Edwin's main areas of research were Arkhium and gravimeters. As his assistant, Jurieu is quite familiar with them as well. I hired him to be my technical consultant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You... you want to blow up the Fortress of Meropide?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Ah, what a lovely idea. I'm already imagining it in my head.

response.speaker: Jurieu
response.text: Gotta admit, I'm tempted as well...

response.speaker: Lourvine
response.text: Guys, focus! Focus!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: That taskmaster over here is Miss Lourvine and is also one of my technical consultants. While Jurieu used to be Edwin's assistant, she used to be Jurieu's assistant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, are they together?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Was that really necessary?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: See, everyone keeps asking this question. Are you two sure you're not a couple, and just using your work as a convenient cover?

response.speaker: Lourvine
response.text: I... Your Grace, I am NOT in a relationship with this man!

response.speaker: Jurieu
response.text: If I dated her, I'd officially be madder than Edwin!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Jeez, forget I said anything, then.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Follow me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, there's another door that goes right up!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Your constant amazement makes it seem like the Fortress can do anything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon really thinks everything's super cool!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is this just a normal room?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Let's spice it up a bit.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: And here you go.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This is...!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a huge... ship?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is also a production zone that Paimon's never seen before... What's going on?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: How much do you know about Fontainian history?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Er... Not much at all...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Then maybe you haven't heard of the story of ancient Remuria. To give you a quick rundown, Fontaine used to be ruled by the Remurian Dynasty.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: According to legend, the Remurian King, Remus, came to this land after being inspired by divine revelation, and found the seer Sybilla, who had taken on the form of a Golden Bee. Taking the Golden Bee with him and riding on a huge ship, the Fortuna, he created his nation above the surging waves.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: He called his nation "Remuria," and used the Fortuna to incessantly search for new tribes and islands, calling on them to join his empire.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a ship in this story, too...?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Where there's water, there will be ships. People believe that hope can always be found at the end of a voyage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you believe that, too?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: To a point, I think. As you've already seen, I have a whole factory's worth of labor, materials, and technology at my disposal. Certainly can't hurt to give it a try.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: So, the moment I began to speculate that the Primordial Sea might lie underneath the gate, I also began this project.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Were you inspired by the legendary Fortuna?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Maybe. Fontainians need something to hold on to to cope with the impending disaster.

choices.text: This is a plan for the ages...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Were the workers to find out the truth behind this ship, riots would destroy the Fortress faster than any catastrophe.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: As the Fortress' administrator, I would never make such a reckless call.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Alright, that's enough talking for now. I'll need another three cups of tea to soothe my throat. Do you have any other questions?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Seems like you're good. Come on, I'll take you back.

choices.text: Can't you share your plan with everyone?

response.speaker: Jurieu
response.text: He's the one who blew the whole Institute sky high. Everyone knew he was a bit crooked in the head, but you're not a local, so I guess it's possible for you not to have heard of him.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I'll leave you here for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Uh... Thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: No worries. But don't forget, it's up to you whether or not you want to share what you just saw. What you do from here on out will likely affect those three as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He means that my actions now will decide the next steps Lyney's group takes.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...In other words, if I want to tell Lyney the truth, I must make him understand that we cannot afford excessive conflict right now.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we'll put a lot of thought into it for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, we will.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Great. I look forward to what happens next.
